The Trump administration has joined Israel in[
launching](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/israel-iran-live-
updates-rcna261099) large-scale attacks across Iran. The strikes mark the
beginning of ​“major combat operations,” according to President Trump, and in
response Tehran has[
reportedly](https://www.cnn.com/2026/02/28/middleeast/israel-attack-iran-intl-
hnk) launched retaliatory attacks in Middle Eastern countries that host U.S.
military bases.

With hundreds of Iranians already killed and the war threatening to spiral out
of control, here are five things Americans need to know.

**1: Trump says he’s trying to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. But
it’s the United States and its allies that are the greatest nuclear threat.**

The United States, not Iran, is the country setting the worst example in
promoting nuclear weapons in the world today.

It was [Trump who pulled out of the U.S.-Iran nuclear deal during his first
term](https://abcnews.com/Politics/iran-nuclear-deal-trump-united-
states/story?id=123020009) — even though the UN
[certified](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/statement-on-iran-
by-the-iaea-spokesperson) that Iran was in compliance — and [resumed harsh
sanctions, deployed more troops to the region](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2019/may/24/us-military-new-troop-middle-east-iran-trump), and [even
assassinated an Iranian general](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-
east-50979463).

Trump’s hostility despite Iran’s earlier compliance only bolsters the claim of
Iranian leaders who believe the country needs nuclear weapons as a deterrent
against aggression.

Meanwhile, Trump just let [the last existing nuclear agreement between the
U.S. and Russia](https://news.northeastern.edu/2026/02/11/start-treaty-us-
russia-nuclear-war/), the two countries with the most warheads, expire. Trump
is also giving unconditional backing to Israel — the  _only_ country in the
Middle East that actually  _has_ nuclear weapons — and is now
[supporting](https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2025-12/news/us-saudi-arabia-
announce-nuclear-cooperation) the launch of a nuclear program in Saudi Arabia.

**2: Trump is contributing to the suffering of ordinary Iranians, not rescuing
them.**

The Iranian government recently carried out a brutal crackdown on protesters
and critics. Trump has claimed that the U.S. is ​“coming to the rescue” of
Iranians who’ve challenged their government.

But in reality, his actions have put countless Iranians in harm’s way.
[Hundreds of civilians have already been killed in the strikes so
far](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/mar/02/civilian-
deaths-in-iran-pass-200-amid-fear-of-bombs-and-regime-clampdown) — including
[165 in an appalling strike on a girl’s
school](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/3/questions-over-minab-girls-
school-strike-as-israel-us-deny-involvement).

Even before the latest violence, U.S. sanctions had [devastated Iran’s
population ](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/13/how-us-sanctions-
crippled-lives-of-iranians-trump-says-he-wants-to-help)— especially women,
children, the sick, people with disabilities, and other vulnerable people —
leading to countless preventable deaths.

**3: The United States is an unreliable negotiator.**

How could Iran — or any country — now take the U.S. seriously at the
negotiating table after Trump blew up the Iran nuclear deal?

Moreover, U.S. demands keep changing. In recent negotiations, [the U.S. kept
moving the goal posts](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/feb/17/iran-us-
nuclear-talks-open-geneva), going from the demand that Iran not develop
nuclear weapons to saying that the country’s civilian nuclear program, its
treatment of dissidents, its relationship with regional allies, and its
[ballistic missile arsenal](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-
east/20260204-us-ready-to-meet-iran-says-rubio-but-talks-must-address-
ballistic-missiles-programme) would all be on the negotiating table.

As Trump [put it bizarrely](https://nypost.com/2026/02/17/world-news/iran-and-
us-agree-guiding-principles-of-nuclear-deal-tehran-says/) on FOX News, the
deal he wants should have ​“no nuclear weapons, no missiles, no this, no that,
all the different things that you want.”

**4: The United States has been threatening Iran, not the other way around.**

Even before the war, [U.S. military bases across the region surrounded
Iran](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/6/12/mapping-us-troops-and-military-
bases-in-the-middle-east) with troops and weapons. But there are no Iranian
troops or military assets anywhere near the United States.

There is also no question that the most aggressive Middle Eastern power at the
moment is Washington’s ally Israel — which continues its [genocide in
Gaza](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2025/09/israel-has-committed-
genocide-gaza-strip-un-commission-finds) and attacked [six other
countries](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/10/maps-israel-has-attacked-
six-countries-in-the-past-72-hours) in the last year alone — all enabled
through military assistance, arms transfers, and political protection by the
United States.

**5: Trump’s war with Iran — and his aggressive foreign policy generally — are
unpopular with Americans.**

The majority of Americans — 61 percent —
[disapprove](https://apnews.com/article/poll-trump-venezuela-foreign-policy-
approval-ce8d92a1461abb354f8c799e6b487e49) of Trump’s aggressive foreign
policy in general. And in a recent  _Reuters_ poll, [just one quarter said
they approved](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/just-one-four-americans-
support-us-strikes-iran-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-03-01/) of Trump’s
decision to strike Iran — and that was  _before_ the announcement that [U.S.
servicemembers had been killed](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/iran-military-
operation-american-service-members-killed-centcom/).

Attacking Iran is not popular, and Trump definitely does not have a mandate to
do it. Whatever criticisms one may have of Iran’s government, they do not
justify this illegal war.
